To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
L20 binds as single monomer to the L20-mRNA bearing two potential binding site.
1) L20 does not form dimers; 2) L20 binds as single monomer to a single binding site on the mRNA; and 3) the two binding sites on the mRNA interact.
1) L20 does not form a dimer, and 2) the L20 mRNA is bound by a single L20 molecule despite the presence of 2 L20-binding sites.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of translation by the ribosomal protein L2O.
the regulation of translation of the L20 mRNA and the mechanism of binding of L20 protein to its own mRNA.
the mechanism by which a single molecule of L20 can repress the translation of its mRNA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
L20 mRNA binds a single L20 molecule and this binding represses translation.
L20 binds to a single site of the L20 mRNA and that this binding is inhibited by the binding of L7/L12 to the 23S ribosome.
L20 binds as one molecule to its own mRNA, and that the two sites are in interaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the binding of one molecule of L 20 to its own mRNA is sufficient for translational repression.
L20 binds to its own mRNA in a single monomer and that this monomer binds to the two L20 sites of the mRNA.
L20 binds as one monomer to a single site on its own mRNA, but that the binding of L 20 to one of the two sites is inhibited by the presence of the other site.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the two sites are in interaction, which is not the case for the L20-binding sites on the 23S rRNA.
the presence of several binding sites for a given RNA-binding protein on the same mRNA does not necessarily mean that the mRNA is bound by several protein molecules.
L20 is able to bind its own mRNA, but only one molecule of protein can bind to the mRNA despite the presence on it of two potential binding motifs.
